title: Song of Solomon 1
paragraphs: ¹ This is the most beautiful of all songs, Solomon's own. ² "Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth — your love is sweeter than wine. ³ The fragrance of your perfumes is intoxicating; your very name is perfume poured out. No wonder all the young women adore you. ⁴ Take me with you — let us run together! The king has brought me into his chambers. We will rejoice and delight in you; we will praise your love above wine. How right they are to love you!" ⁵ "I am dark and beautiful, O daughters of Jerusalem — dark as the tents of Kedar, lovely as the curtains of Solomon."

⁶ Don't look down on me because I am dark, because the sun has bronzed my skin. My mother's sons were angry with me; they made me tend the vineyards — my own vineyard I could not tend. ⁷ Tell me, you whom I love with all my heart — where do you graze your flock? Where do you rest them at midday? Why should I wander like a veiled woman among the flocks of your companions?" ⁸ "If you don't know, O most beautiful of women, go out and follow the tracks of the sheep; graze your young goats near the shepherds' tents. ⁹ I compare you, my love, to a mare among Pharaoh's chariots. ¹⁰ Your cheeks are lovely framed in jewels, your neck beautiful in strings of beads."

¹¹ "We will make you gold earrings studded with silver." ¹² While the king is at his table, my perfume fills the air with its fragrance. ¹³ My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh resting between my breasts through the night. ¹⁴ My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms from the vineyards of Engedi. ¹⁵ "How beautiful you are, my love! How beautiful — your eyes are doves."
¹⁶ "How beautiful you are, my beloved, how delightful! Our bed is a bed of green. ¹⁷ The beams of our house are cedar; our rafters are fir."
